51121411.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to recombinant human flag/His-tagged IL-23R (1 to 353 residues) expressed in HEK293F cells measured over 90 secs by surface plasmon resonance assay
51121411.references_previous: Bloch, Y.; Bouchareych, L.; Merceron, R.; Skladanowska, K.; Vega, F.; Yu, N.; Wang, J.; Singh, K.; Zonin, F.; Vaisberg, E.; Churakova, J.; Liu, M.; Gorman, D.; Wagner, J.; Zurawski, G.; Liu, Y.; Abrams, J. S.; Moore, K. W.; Rennick, D.; de Waal-Malefyt, R.; Hannum, C.; Bazan, J. F.; Kastelein, R. A. Novel p19 protein engages IL-12p40 to form a cytokine, IL-23, with biological activities similar as well as distinct from IL-12. Immunity 2000, 13, 715–725.

original_paragraph.Figure 1 caption: Figure 1. Schematic based on Bloch et al.6 showing the domains of IL-23R (orange), the p19 helical bundle of IL-23 (blue), the three domains of IL-23p40 (green, structurally identical to IL-12p40), and the binding site of compound C on D1 of IL-23R as identified in this paper (red star). The membrane (brown) and putative location of IL-12Rβ1 (light gray, required along with IL-23R to form the full IL-23 receptor complex) are also shown (A). Structure of the macrocyclic dodecapeptide inhibitor C of IL-23R (B). SPR Sensorgrams (colors) of different concentrations of Compound C against IL-23R and their fit (black) to a 1:1 binding model (C). SPR revealed the following binding parameters: ka = 1.51 × 107 (1/Ms), kd = 2.74 × 10-2 (1/s), KD = 1.81 (nM). Because of the limited curvature observed from the sensorgrams, the SPR binding experiment appeared to be mass transport limited. Therefore, the binding parameters should be considered an estimate.
